Ingredient Directory

Vegetables

About Vegetables

Vegetables organized by culinary groups — how they're used in the kitchen, not botanical classification: Alliums, Green Vegetables, Root Vegetables & Squash, and Nightshades.

Explore Vegetables

  • Alliums — Alliums are sulfur-rich aromatics that form the flavor base of countless savory dishes, including onion, garlic, and shallot.
  • Green Vegetables — Green vegetables cover leafy greens, stems, and green pods central to savory cooking, from delicate spinach to sturdy kale.
  • Nightshades — Nightshades bring bold color and flavor to savory cooking, including tomato, eggplant, and pepper-class vegetables.
  • Root Vegetables — Root vegetables and squash covers earthy roots and winter squash used in roasting, braising, and long-cooked dishes, including carrots, beets, turnips, and winter squash.
